name: Mass MFA Disable from Helpdesk Console
description: Helpdesk technician (or someone using their session) walks down a list of 41 VIP accounts and clicks 'reset MFA / require re-enrollment' in 30 minutes. Real CEO travelling overseas and four other execs go from MFA-required to no-MFA right before a phishing wave hits.
reasoning: Identity provider (Entra/Okta-style) is the affected service. The signal is repeated 'MFA reset' admin actions from one principal in a tight window, against a list that doesn't match normal helpdesk ticket flow.

narrative.text: Quiet baseline. Helpdesk averages ~3 MFA resets/hour during business hours.
13:14 UTC — admin 't.harris@corp' starts running 'Reset MFA factors' on a list of 41 accounts.
By 13:32 — 28 resets done; targets are concentrated in C-suite + finance, not the day's tickets.
Phishing emails land in the affected mailboxes within minutes — 'Verify your new login' lure.
All 41 accounts force-reset to require MFA again; t.harris session terminated; investigation opens.
Forensics: helpdesk session token had been replayed from an unfamiliar IP for ~14 hours.
All affected users re-onboarded onto FIDO2; helpdesk session-binding policy tightened.

okta.note: MFA bulk reset by admin session
